text: I haven't had any abdominal pain recently, but I did have a severe episode of upper abdominal pain three years ago. Since then, I have been experiencing yellowing of my skin, intense itching, and significant weight loss. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor

text: RESULTS: Liver Function Tests: Total Bilirubin 5.6 mg/dL (Elevated), Direct Bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL (Elevated), Alkaline Phosphatase 192 U/L (Elevated), AST 32 U/L (Normal), ALT 34 U/L (Normal). Abdominal Ultrasound: Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region with dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of a cystic mass with bile duct dilation, combined with your painless jaundice and history of prior abdominal pain, strongly suggest a choledochal cyst. I will proceed with further imaging to confirm the anatomy and rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP results contradict the ultrasound findings of a cystic mass and bile duct dilation, which is highly unusual. Could you clarify if you have had any recent surgeries, such as a cholecystectomy, or if there is a history of liver disease in your family?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have never had any surgeries, and there is no known history of liver disease in my family. I am quite confused by these conflicting test results, but my symptoms of yellow skin and dark urine have persisted for the past two weeks.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the conflicting imaging results and your specific symptoms, I need to rule out a malignancy that might have been missed or misinterpreted. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Abdomen/Pelvis: A well-defined, thin-walled cystic structure arising from the common bile duct, causing upstream dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree. No evidence of solid mass or malignancy. Findings are consistent with a Type I choledochal cyst.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan confirms a Type I choledochal cyst, which explains your obstructive jaundice, pruritus, and pale stools. I will now proceed to finalize the diagnosis based on these definitive imaging results. DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledochal Cyst
